entries.question: Jupiter and Saturn are called “gas giants.” Just how much bigger are they than rocky planets like Earth and Mars?
Summer days in Fort Wayne have almost 6 more hours of daylight than winter days. It’s NOT because Earth is closer to the Sun — so what causes it?
In 1944, 29 reindeer were released on a remote Alaskan island with plenty of food and NO predators. The herd exploded to 6,000 — then almost vanished. What happened?
Why is a rainforest bursting with thousands of species while a desert or frozen tundra has so few? Two things about climate explain most of it.
Ocean buoys measure wave height during storms. A wave twice as tall carries far more than twice the energy — so how does a storm's wave height line up with the energy pounding the shore?
Shine the same flashlight through clear glass, frosted glass, and cardboard. Why does one glow through, one glows dimly, and one stays dark?
Put a water plant under brighter and brighter lamps and count the oxygen bubbles it makes. Does more light always mean more photosynthesis?
Why does a grassland have thousands of grass plants, lots of grasshoppers, fewer mice, and only a handful of hawks? Follow the energy up the pyramid.
In 1995, scientists released 41 wolves into Yellowstone after 70 years with none. What happened to the elk the wolves hunt?
A class is designing a lunchbox that keeps food cold. Before building, they rated how important each goal was. Which needs matter most, and which are just nice to have?
Ever heard an old radio hiss and fade, but a digital song stay crystal clear? As a signal travels farther and picks up static, which type survives — analog or digital?
In the Antarctic ocean, tiny krill feed almost everything bigger. What share of a predator community's diet comes from krill versus other foods?
On a guitar, a short tight string sounds high and a long loose string sounds low. How does the length of a sound wave relate to how many waves pass each second?
Seal a leafy plant in a sunny jar and measure the air. What happens to carbon dioxide and oxygen over a few hours as the plant makes food?
After zebra mussels sneaked into the Great Lakes, native mussels started vanishing. How fast did the invader take over — and what did it do to the natives?
Press your ear to a metal railing and tap the far end — you hear it almost instantly. Why does sound race through steel and water but crawl through air?
Three phone-case designs each score well on some goals and poorly on others. If no case wins on everything, which one best fits what users care about most?
Bury identical apple slices in different spots and check them weekly. Where do decomposers break down matter fastest — and why does that matter for an ecosystem?
A buoy recorded 100 ocean waves in one hour. Most were medium-sized, but a few were surprisingly tall. How often does a really big wave show up?
Two identical bean seedlings start the same size. One gets full sunlight, one gets dim light. After three weeks, how differently have they grown — and why?
The planets closest to the Sun race around it, while the far ones crawl. Plot each planet's orbital speed against its distance and figure out why the Sun's grip loosens with distance.
Some planets have zero moons and some have dozens. Compare the number of confirmed moons for each planet and see whether bigger planets tend to collect more.
On the shortest day of winter, Fort Wayne gets barely nine hours of daylight; in June it gets over fifteen. Plot daylight hours across the year and connect the pattern to Earth's tilt.
When wolves returned to Yellowstone in 1995, the huge elk herds began to shrink. Plot wolf and elk numbers on the same timeline and decide how much the wolves were responsible.
Some species help each other, some fight, and some just take. Compare how common each kind of interaction is in a sample of studied species pairs and see which relationship dominates.
Jupiter is so wide that eleven Earths could line up across it, while Mercury is barely bigger than our Moon. Use icons to compare planet diameters and feel the enormous range.
A class built four homemade water filters and measured how cloudy the water still was afterward. Compare the test results and decide which design solution actually works best.
Farmers who rent beehives often harvest far more fruit per acre. Compare crop yields with and without pollinators and weigh whether the ecosystem service is worth paying for.
On one Galápagos island, finches with different beak sizes eat different seeds. Plot beak depth against the hardness of seeds each bird can crack and find the pattern that lets them share the island.
A day on Jupiter is under 10 hours, but a single day on Venus lasts longer than its whole year. Compare how long one spin takes on each planet and hunt for the oddball.
In a dry grassland, wetter years grow more plants — and more plants mean more rabbits. Plot yearly rainfall against the rabbit population and see how tightly food controls their numbers.
Divers counted fish species at four reef sites — some healthy, some damaged. Compare the spread of counts and decide which reef design solution best protects biodiversity.
Over about a month the Moon swells from a sliver to full and back. Plot the percent of the Moon lit each night and match the curve to the phase names.
An engineering team tested four cup insulators by measuring temperature, cost, weight, and how long the drink stayed hot. Compare the profiles and pick the design that balances every trade-off.
The farther a planet orbits, the longer its year — but the jump is bigger than distance alone. Plot orbital distance against year length and see how dramatically the outer planets fall behind.
Tiny cleaner wrasse pick parasites off bigger fish that could easily eat them — yet both benefit. Compare parasite loads before and after a cleaning station opens and prove the partnership pays off.
In 2010, coal produced almost half of U.S. electricity. By 2023 it had collapsed. What replaced it — and is our electricity getting cleaner?
A car going 20 m/s does NOT have just twice the energy of a car going 10 m/s. Use the graph to find out how much more it really has.
You hang weights on a spring and measure how far it stretches. Is there a rule connecting the force you add and the stretch you get?
When you hear about earthquakes in the news, they’re usually big ones. But are powerful earthquakes actually common — or rare? Plot a week of them and find out.
It takes water to grow food — but some foods take WAY more than others. How much water is hidden in the different parts of your dinner?
There is no perfect water bottle — every design is great at some things and weak at others. Which one “wins” depends on what you care about most. Compare three.
A trampoline stretched twice as far does NOT store just twice the energy. Use the graph to see how fast stored energy climbs as a spring is stretched.
A roller-coaster car lifted to the top of a tall hill stores energy just from being up high. Use the graph to find how stored energy grows with height.
Astronauts far above Earth still feel gravity, but weaker. Use the graph to see how quickly gravity's pull drops as you move away from Earth.
A 60 kg astronaut weighs very different amounts on different worlds — same body, same mass. Use the graph to compare surface gravity across the solar system.
Heating a full pot of water takes far more energy than heating a cupful, even to the same temperature. Use the graph to see how energy needed grows with the amount of water.
Beach sand gets scorching at noon while the ocean stays cool — same sunshine. Use the graph to see why some materials heat up so much faster than water.
An engineer tests four cup designs to keep coffee hot. Use the graph to decide which design best minimizes thermal energy transfer over 30 minutes.
Push a cart harder over the same distance and it speeds up more. Use the graph to see how a cart's kinetic energy changes as speed increases.
When a small car crashes into a big truck, which pushes harder on the other? Use the graph of a collision to check whether the forces are really equal and opposite.
A refrigerator magnet grabs hard when touching but barely pulls from a centimeter away. Use the graph to see how magnetic force fades with distance.
Junkyard cranes lift cars with electromagnets and drop them by cutting the current. Use the graph to see how more current makes an electromagnet stronger.
Rub a balloon on your hair and it pulls tiny paper bits without touching them. Use the graph to see how this at-a-distance electric force weakens with separation.
Engineers test five wall materials to keep a house warm in winter. Use the graph to rank which materials lose the least heat.
A bowling ball and a ping-pong ball at the same speed are very different to stop. Use the graph to compare the momentum each object carries into a collision.
Earth, a magnet, and a charged balloon all reach out through empty space. Use the graph to compare how three kinds of fields fade as you move away from their source.
You can't see a single cell with your eyes — but not all cells are the same size. Some are thousands of times bigger than others. How much do cells really vary?
A single cell is like a tiny factory, and its organelles are the machines. But which parts take up the most space inside a typical cell?
Your body is a team of systems, and each one is built from a different number of organs and parts. How do the major organ systems compare in scale?
Your body rearranges food molecules to release energy. But some foods store far more chemical energy per bite than others. How much do everyday foods differ?
When a light flashes, your eyes sense it, your brain processes it, and your hand reacts — all in a fraction of a second. But reaction time changes as we age. How does it shift across a lifetime?
Earth is about 4.6 billion years old, but life as we know it fills only a sliver of that story. How is Earth's vast history divided among its major eons and eras?
Rivers, waves, and wind slowly wear the land down — but not everywhere at the same speed. How different are erosion rates around the world?

The ocean floor is like a conveyor belt: new rock forms at mid-ocean ridges and gets older as it moves away. If plates really spread, seafloor age should grow steadily with distance from a ridge. Does it?
Rocks are constantly recycled between three types, but they aren't spread evenly. Most of what we walk on is one kind, while most of Earth's crust is another. What makes up the crust?
A class of students each tested how fast they could catch a dropped ruler. No two people were exactly the same. What did the whole class's reaction times look like together?
Your body releases food energy and spends it on everything you do — even resting. But some activities burn stored energy far faster than others. How much do they differ?
Long ago, the continents were joined in one supercontinent. If that's true, the same fossils and rocks should show up on coastlines now separated by oceans. How well does the evidence line up?
Rivers pick up rock and soil upstream and drop it downstream, reshaping the land. Some of the world's great rivers move staggering amounts of sediment to the sea each year. How do they compare?
Every living thing is made of cells — but a tiny ant is built from a few billion while a whale has tens of trillions. How wildly does cell count vary across animals?
Earth's plates are moving right now — about as fast as your fingernails grow. But some plates race ahead while others creep. How different are their speeds?
Earth’s average temperature has climbed sharply since about 1980. What questions should scientists ask to figure out the cause?
Two shiny metal blocks look alike — one is aluminum, one is iron. With no labels, how could mass and volume tell them apart?
You measure 50 bean seeds from the same variety of plant. They’re all “the same kind” of bean — so why isn’t every seed the same length?
Fort Wayne summers and winters feel completely different. A box plot compares not just the average temperature each season, but how much it swings day to day. Which season is the most unpredictable?
Earth is the “water planet” — but if you’re thirsty, almost none of it is usable. Where is all of Earth’s water actually stored?
A climograph shows two things at once for every month — how warm it is (the line) and how much it rains (the bars). What kind of climate does central Indiana have?
A country’s “population pyramid” shows how many people are young versus old. A wide base means lots of children — and rapid growth still to come. What does this shape predict?

These five common molecules all contain the same few kinds of atoms, but in very different counts. Which molecule packs in the most atoms per formula unit, and does having more atom types always mean more atoms?
Drop cork, ice, aluminum, and gold into water and some float while others sink like a stone. Density — the mass packed into each cubic centimeter — decides. How do these substances compare?
You heat a beaker of ice at a steady rate until it becomes steam. The temperature climbs, then stalls, climbs, then stalls again. Why does adding energy sometimes NOT raise the temperature?
A sealed flask holds reactants that combine into products. When you weigh the flask before and after the reaction, the total mass is identical. Where did the atoms go?
You drop the same antacid tablet into water at different temperatures and time how long it takes to fully dissolve. Warmer water dissolves it faster. What is temperature doing to the particles?
Most plastics are made from petroleum. This chart shows where a barrel of refined crude oil ends up. What fraction goes toward the raw materials for synthetic products like plastics?

An instant cold pack works because dissolving a salt absorbs heat from its surroundings. This chart shows how much the temperature drops for different salts. Which salt would you choose to design the coldest pack?
Some animals lay thousands of eggs and walk away; others have one baby and guard it fiercely. This chart compares how many young each animal has per year. How can such different strategies both work?
Identical bean seedlings were grown under different daily amounts of light for three weeks. Their final heights differ dramatically. How much does light drive plant growth, and is more always better?

Two groups of genetically identical corn plants were grown in nutrient-rich versus nutrient-poor soil. Their final heights are spread out below. How does the environment shift the growth of plants that share the same genes?
Your body is built from atoms, but just a handful of elements make up almost all of it. This pictograph shows the most common elements by mass. Which few elements account for nearly everything?
Every pure substance melts at a characteristic temperature. This chart compares the melting points of several common substances. Could you use melting point alone to tell two unknown solids apart?

Temperature is a measure of how fast particles move. This graph shows the average speed of gas particles at different temperatures on the Kelvin scale. What happens to particle motion as things heat up?

A reusable hand warmer releases heat when sodium acetate crystallizes. This graph tracks the temperature of the pack after it is triggered. How quickly does it warm up, and how long does the heat last?

Many birds migrate to survive winter and reach breeding grounds. This dot plot shows the day in spring that individual robins were first seen arriving at a nesting site. When do most robins arrive, and why might timing matter for survival?
After the 1977 drought on Daphne Major left mostly large, hard seeds, the surviving medium ground finches were not a random sample of the old population. How did the range of beak depths change?

As soot from factories darkened tree bark near industrial English cities in the 1800s, the peppered moth population changed color. How common did the dark form become before pollution controls reversed the trend?
The fossil record preserves five major mass extinctions across geologic time. In which of these events did the largest share of marine animal species disappear?
A human arm, a cat leg, a whale flipper, and a bat wing all do different jobs, yet share the same underlying bone plan. How similar are their forelimb skeletons?
For over 100 generations, researchers at the Illinois Long-Term Selection Experiment bred only the corn kernels with the highest oil content. How far did the oil level climb?
When bacteria are grown with an antibiotic, most die but a few resistant cells survive and multiply. How does the share of resistant bacteria change as the drug keeps being used?
Early vertebrate embryos share features that adults do not, such as a tail and pharyngeal (throat) arches. Across five animals, how many of these shared embryo traits appear?
A single DNA mutation can change a protein and, through it, an organism's trait. In a beetle population, mutations produce three different wing-case phenotypes. How common is each?
In a population of mice living on dark volcanic rock, hawks pick off the light-colored mice. Over several generations, how does the spread of fur-darkness scores change?
A town added a filter to a factory to reduce nitrate pollution in a river, then placed sensors upstream and downstream to check whether it worked. What do the readings show?
The horse fossil record spans over 50 million years, from dog-sized ancestors to today's horse. How did shoulder height change across these fossil forms?
In streams with many predators, brightly spotted male guppies get eaten more often, while in safe pools bright spots help attract mates. How does spot size differ between these two settings?
When scientists count how many trilobite species appear in each rock layer, the numbers rise and then crash. What story do the layers tell about this group?

Beyond bones, scientists compare the protein cytochrome c across species. The more amino-acid differences from humans, the more distantly related the animal tends to be. How do these differences line up?
